subject: Anthropology
title: Speech Communities
description: Learn Speech Communities in one minute.

hook.text: A group of skaters has its own slang. So does Wall Street. Each group builds a shared way of talking.

buildup.text: A speech community is a group that shares linguistic norms, vocabulary, and ways of using language.

discovery.text: Membership isn't about where you live but who you interact with. Online communities create new speech norms too.

twist.text: Everyone belongs to multiple speech communities simultaneously — family, work, friends — and shifts between them.

climax.text: Speech communities show that language is social glue. Shared ways of talking create belonging and identity.

quiz.question: What defines a speech community?
options: Sharing linguistic norms and ways of using language

details.summary: A speech community is a group that shares language norms and expectations about how language should be used. Members may speak different languages but share rules about when, where, and how to use them in social contexts.
details.whyItMatters: The concept of speech community shifts focus from language as an abstract system to language as social practice. It emphasizes that communication depends on shared norms, not just shared vocabulary.
takeaways: Speech communities share norms about appropriate language use
Members may speak different languages but share usage conventions
The concept emphasizes language as social practice over abstract system

faq.question: Is a speech community the same as a group speaking one language?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A multilingual community where everyone knows when to use which language constitutes a speech community through shared norms. Conversely, English speakers in London and Delhi may share a language but differ in communicative norms and expectations.

faq.question: How do speech communities maintain their norms?
faq.answer: Through social feedback — approving appropriate language use and correcting or stigmatizing inappropriate use. Children learn norms through socialization. Adults who violate community norms face social consequences ranging from confusion to exclusion.
